title: Jensen Huang on Nvidia's 33 years: first principles, empty chairs, character forged by suffering
summary: Jensen explains how he reasons from first principles, runs about 60 direct reports, refuses to fill a chair with the wrong person, and builds corporate character through shared pain. He also covers ignorance as a superpower, CEO vulnerability, and why AI makes problems look smaller and people busier.

principles.text: Build belief on first principles, then keep re-checking that the foundation is still sound; if it changes, re-evaluate and move on.
principles.quote: You have to reason through for what reason do you believe this and break down um your reasoning into into sound first principles and and then you have to you have to check it on a regular basis

principles.text: Inventing technology is not enough; you must also invent products, strategies, and the market itself.
principles.quote: You have to shape the market to receive your products that you invented and the strategies that you developed

principles.text: Never fill a chair with the wrong person; the company keeps moving, so wait for the right one.
principles.quote: an empty empty chair is better than a chair filled with the wrong person and so I'm never in a hurry.

principles.text: Great companies are defined by corporate character, forged by enduring pain together, not by intelligence or hard work alone.
principles.quote: it's just corporate character and that character comes from somewhere. That's what defines great companies.

principles.text: Make speed so large that a phase change happens: when computing gets vastly faster, hard problems look small.
principles.quote: when the tool when the instrument when the tool is way way faster then the problem looks way smaller

principles.text: Ignorance and optimism are superpowers for founders; approach hard things with 'how hard can it be?'
principles.quote: I approached everything with this attitude how hard can it be?
